title: CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death

paragraphs.en: Marilla's alarmed voice echoed through the house: "Matthew—Matthew—what is the matter? Matthew, are you sick?" Anne rushed in with white narcissus, her hands full.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉焦急的声音在屋子里回荡：“马修——马修——出什么事了？马修，你生病了吗？”安妮手里拿着几朵白水仙匆匆跑进来。

paragraphs.en: Before she could reach him, Marilla saw Matthew standing by the door, pale and drawn, holding a folded paper.
paragraphs.zh: 在她还没来得及靠近他之前，玛丽拉看到马修站在门口，面色苍白憔悴，手里拿着一张折叠好的纸。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew has fainted," gasped Marilla. "Anne, run for Martin—quickly! He's at the barn."
paragraphs.zh: “马修晕过去了，”玛丽拉喘着气说，“安妮，快去叫马汀！他在谷仓里。”

paragraphs.en: Martin, just back from the post office, was sent to fetch the doctor while Mrs. Lynde joined them. They found Anne and Marilla trying desperately to revive Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: 马丁刚从邮局回来，被派去请医生，而雷切尔·林德夫人则加入了他们。他们发现安妮和玛丽拉正竭力想唤醒马修。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Lynde gently pushed them aside, checked his pulse, and listened to his heart. Her face showed sorrow as she said, "I don't think we can do anything for him."
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔·林德夫人轻轻推开他们，检查了马修的脉搏，又听了听他的心跳。她脸上带着悲伤的表情说：“我想我们对他已经无能为力了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne turned pale at the thought of death. The doctor arrived and confirmed that Matthew had died instantly, likely from a sudden shock. The paper in Matthew's hand revealed the cause: the failure of Abbey Bank.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮一想到死亡就变得面色苍白。医生赶到后确认，马修瞬间离世，可能是由于突如其来的惊吓所致。马修手中的那份文件揭示了原因：埃文利银行倒闭了。

paragraphs.en: News spread quickly through Avonlea. Friends and neighbors came to Green Gables all day, offering their condolences and assistance. Quiet Matthew Cuthbert suddenly became central; death had set him apart as someone important.
paragraphs.zh: 埃文利很快便传开了这个消息。朋友们和邻居们一整天都来到绿山墙农舍，表达他们的同情并提供帮助。平时安静的马修突然成了众人关注的焦点；死亡让他变得至关重要。

paragraphs.en: On a calm night at Green Gables, Matthew Cuthbert lay in his coffin in the parlor. Anne had placed sweet old-fashioned flowers around him—flowers her mother had planted long ago. She stood by the window, holding back tears as she brought the flowers to him.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个宁静的夜晚，马修·库伯在绿山墙农舍的客厅里躺在了他的棺材中。安妮在他周围摆放了芳香的老式花朵——这些花是她母亲多年前种植的。她站在窗前，强忍着泪水，将鲜花递给了他。

paragraphs.en: Diana approached and asked gently, "Anne dear, would you like me to sleep with you tonight?"
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜走近，轻声问道：“安妮心爱的，今晚你想要我和你一起睡吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Thank you, Diana," Anne replied earnestly. "I need to be alone for a while."
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢你，戴安娜，”安妮认真地说，“我需要独处一会儿。”

paragraphs.en: That night, Anne kept vigil in her room, trying to accept Matthew's death. She felt both that he couldn't be dead and that it had been long since his passing. The dull ache of sorrow persisted.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，安妮独自守在房里，试图接受马修去世的事实。她心里既觉得他不可能真的离世，又意识到他已经离开很久了。悲伤的钝痛依旧挥之不去。

paragraphs.en: Marilla's intense grief overwhelmed Anne’s silent pain. Diana left Anne alone, allowing her the solitude she sought.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉深切的悲痛淹没了安妮默默的哀伤。戴安娜让安妮独自一人，让她得以享受她所渴望的孤独。

paragraphs.en: In darkness, Anne knelt by her window, praying to the stars beyond the hills. Despite her love for Matthew and his kindness, no tears came at first. Only the persistent dull ache of misery lingered until exhaustion finally overcame her.
paragraphs.zh: 在黑暗中，安妮跪在窗前，仰望着山那边的星星祈祷。尽管她深爱着马修，并且他也很善良，但她起初并没有流下眼泪。只有那种持久而沉闷的痛苦折磨着她，直到精疲力尽终于将她克服。

paragraphs.en: Anne woke in the night, feeling the stillness and darkness around her. She remembered Matthew’s smile from their last parting and his proud words. Tears filled her eyes as she wept deeply.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在夜半时分醒来，感受到四周的寂静与黑暗。她想起了马修上次分别时的笑容和他的自豪话语。泪水涌上眼眶，她不禁深深哭泣起来。

paragraphs.en: Marilla heard Anne's sobs and entered to comfort her.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉听见安妮的抽泣声，走进来安慰她。

paragraphs.en: "There—there—don't cry so much, dearie. It won't bring him back. I know it isn't right to cry this way, but I couldn't help it.
paragraphs.zh: “别哭得这么厉害，亲爱的。这不会让他回来的。我知道这样哭不对，但我控制不住自己。”

paragraphs.en: He was always such a good brother. God knows best."
paragraphs.zh: 他总是这么好的哥哥。上帝最清楚了。

paragraphs.en: Anne sobbed, "Just let me cry, Marilla. The tears don’t hurt as much as the pain does. Stay here with me and hold me—like that.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮抽泣着说：“让我哭一会儿吧，玛丽拉。眼泪虽然痛苦，却比那种痛楚好受些。你留下来陪我，在我身边抱着我——就像这样。”

paragraphs.en: Diana is kind and sweet, but she’s outside our sorrow. She can't come close enough to help. It's ours—yours and mine."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜心地善良，温柔可人，但她却在我们的悲伤之外。她无法走近，给予帮助。这悲伤属于我们——你和我。

paragraphs.en: Marilla comforted her, "We have each other, Anne. I don’t know what I’d do without you. You’ve been my joy and comfort since you came to Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉安慰她说：“我们有彼此，安妮。我不知道没有你会怎么办。自从你来到绿山墙，你就一直是我的欢乐和慰藉。”

paragraphs.en: Maybe I've been strict with you, but I loved you as much as Matthew did."
paragraphs.zh: 也许我对你的要求有些严格，但我的爱并不会比马修少。

paragraphs.en: Two days later, Matthew Cuthbert was carried over his homestead threshold. He left behind fields he had tilled and orchards he loved. Avonlea returned to its usual calm, and Green Gables resumed their routine.
paragraphs.zh: 两天后，马修·库特伯格被抬过了自家门槛。他留下了辛勤劳作的田地和心爱的果园。埃文利镇恢复了往日的宁静，绿山墙农舍也重新恢复了日常的生活节奏。

paragraphs.en: Anne, new to grief, found it almost sad that life continued as before without him.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮对悲伤还很陌生，发现没有他的日子里生活依旧如常进行，这让她感到几乎有些伤感。

paragraphs.en: "It seems like disloyalty to Matthew," she said wistfully to Mrs. Allan one evening in the manse garden. "I miss him so much, yet I find pleasure in sunrises and Diana's visits."
paragraphs.zh: “对马修来说，这似乎是一种不忠，”她依依不舍地对艾伦太太说。一个傍晚，在牧师园子里，她说，“我如此怀念他，却又在日出和戴安娜的来访中找到了乐趣。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan gently reminded her, "Matthew liked hearing you laugh and finding joy in nature. He would want you to enjoy these things even now that he is gone."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮温柔地提醒说：“马修喜欢听你笑，喜欢在自然中寻找乐趣。即使他不在了，他也希望你能继续享受这些美好。”

paragraphs.en: Anne felt conflicted. "Today Diana said something funny, and I laughed. I thought I could never do that again.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮内心矛盾起来。“今天戴安娜说了一句有趣的话，我忍不住笑了。我以为自己再也不会这么做。

paragraphs.en: It feels as if I should not."
paragraphs.zh: 我觉得自己恐怕不行了。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan understood her feelings. "We all experience this. We resent finding pleasure when someone we love is no longer here to share it with us.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉理解安妮的感受：“我们都有这样的体会。当我们所爱的人不在了，却还在享受着快乐时，我们会感到不满。”

paragraphs.en: But nature offers healing, and we shouldn't shut our hearts against its influences."
paragraphs.zh: 但是大自然能带来治愈，我们不应关闭心灵，拒绝接受它的影响。

paragraphs.en: Anne went to the graveyard to plant a rosebush on Matthew's grave. She took a slip of the small white Scotch roses his mother had brought from Scotland, as they always pleased him. Anne hoped he would have these roses in heaven and that their souls were there to greet him.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮来到墓地，在马修的坟前种下了一株玫瑰。她选取了母亲从苏格兰带来的几朵小白花石竹，因为这些花总是让马修感到欢喜。安妮希望他在天堂里能见到这些玫瑰，并且相信他们的灵魂会在那里迎接他。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan said Anne would make Marilla lonelier when she left for college again. Anne did not reply; instead, she sat beside Marilla on the front doorsteps. The open door was held by a big pink conch shell with hints of sea sunsets inside.
paragraphs.zh: 艾伦太太说，安妮再次去上大学时肯定会让玛丽拉感到更加孤独。安妮没有回答，而是坐在了玛丽拉身旁，靠在前门廊的台阶上。敞开的门由一个大号粉色海螺壳撑开着，里面仿佛映射着海上的落日余晖。

paragraphs.en: Anne gathered some pale-yellow honeysuckle and placed them in her hair, enjoying their fragrance as an aerial benediction. Marilla mentioned that Doctor Spencer had visited while Anne was away and insisted she go to town for an eye examination the next day. She asked Anne to stay alone at Green Gables and promised to have Martin drive her.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮摘了一些淡黄色的野蔷薇花插在头发里，享受着它们带来的淡淡香气，仿佛这是一种天赐的祝福。玛丽拉提到斯宾塞医生在安妮外出期间来访，并坚持要求安妮第二天去镇上进行眼睛检查。她让安妮独自留在绿山墙农舍，并承诺会让马丁开车送她去医院。

paragraphs.en: Anne assured Marilla she would be fine, adding that Diana would visit for company. She said she would handle ironing and baking without any mishaps. Marilla laughed, recalling how Anne used to make mistakes and get into scrapes.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮向玛丽拉保证自己会没事，并提到戴安娜会来陪她。她说自己会处理熨衣和烘焙，不会出任何差错。玛丽拉笑了笑，回忆起安妮过去常常犯错误、惹麻烦的情景。

paragraphs.en: Anne smiled as she touched her neatly braided hair. "I used to worry about it so much, but now I laugh a little. It was a real trouble back then."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮摸了摸她梳理得整整齐齐的头发，笑了笑：“以前我可为此操心了不少，但现在我会微微一笑。那确实是一段烦恼的日子。”

paragraphs.en: She added, "Josie Pye still thinks my hair is redder than ever, which makes me frustrated."
paragraphs.zh: 她补充说：“乔西·派伊还认为我的头发比以前更红了，这让我感到很沮丧。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla sharply replied, "Josie is a Pye, and she can't help being disagreeable. I don’t know what useful purpose people like her serve in society." Marilla continued, "Josie won't teach next year; Moody Spurgeon and Charlie Sloane are going back to Queen's. Jane and Ruby will teach—Jane at Newbridge, and Ruby somewhere west."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉尖刻地回答道：“乔西是派，她天生就不太讨人喜欢。我不知道这种人在社会里有什么用处。”接着，玛丽拉继续说道：“乔西明年不会再来教书了；莫迪·斯普劳尔和查理·斯洛恩要回女王学院。简和露比会来教书——简在纽伯里，露比则会在西部某个地方任教。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla then asked, "Is Gilbert Blythe teaching too?"
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉接着问道：“吉尔伯特·布莱斯也开始当老师了吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes," Anne replied briefly.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”安妮简洁地回答道。

paragraphs.en: "Such a nice-looking fellow," Marilla said absentmindedly. "I saw him in church last Sunday; he seemed tall and manly. He looks like his father did at the same age."
paragraphs.zh: “真是个英俊的小伙子，”玛丽拉若有所思地说，“我上星期天在教堂见过他；他个子挺高，看上去很有男子气概。他的确像他父亲年轻时的样子。”

paragraphs.en: She added, "John Blythe was a good friend."
paragraphs.zh: 她补充道：“约翰·布雷思是一位很好的朋友。”

paragraphs.en: Anne's eyes widened with interest. "Marilla—what happened? Why didn't you forgive him?"
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的眼睛里闪烁着好奇的光芒。“玛丽拉——发生了什么事？你怎么不原谅他呢？”

paragraphs.en: Marilla explained, "We had a quarrel. I wouldn’t forgive him when he asked me to. I meant to later but was too sulky and angry.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉解释说：“我们吵了一架。他求我原谅时，我没有答应。本来打算后来原谅他的，但当时气得要命，郁郁不欢。”

paragraphs.en: He never came back—the Blythes were independent. But I always felt sorry for not forgiving him."
paragraphs.zh: 他再也没回来——布赖斯一家独立自主。但我总是为自己没有宽恕他而感到遗憾。

paragraphs.en: Anne softly said, "So you've had your share of romance too."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮轻声说道：“原来你也有过浪漫的经历啊。”

paragraphs.en: I suppose you could call it that. You wouldn't guess by looking at me, but people are unpredictable. Everyone had forgotten about John and me, even me.
paragraphs.zh: 我想你可以说这是命运的安排。单从外表看，你可能不会猜到这一点，但人们总是难以预料。就连我自己也被大家遗忘了。

paragraphs.en: But seeing Gilbert last Sunday brought everything back.
paragraphs.zh: 但上周日见到吉尔伯特后，往事全都涌上心头。
